content:
Earlier this month, OpenAI launched its first GPT-6 model alongside Astra. The GPT-6 series has officially released two new models, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, continuing to expand its lineup.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are available starting today

According to the update notes for the ChatGPT desktop app, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna consume fewer tokens than their GPT-5.6 counterparts.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are being rolled out gradually on Codex and ChatGPT Work, with token pricing lower than the previous-generation GPT-5.6. Sol is suited for handling complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna is designed for tasks requiring high focus and high throughput. Both models will be made available in phases to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna via the desktop app. Actual availability depends on rollout progress and workspace settings; Enterprise administrators will need to enable the new models themselves. Within ChatGPT, both models are currently available only on Work and Codex, and have not yet landed on Chat.

Worth noting: there is no so-called GPT-6 Terra. It appears OpenAI is gradually phasing out mid-tier specs, keeping only three tiers: Terra (small), Sol (large), and Astra (extra-large).

Below is the official announcement from OpenAI:

Even though the toughest, most impactful work still requires the full depth of Astra, different tasks come with different scales, paces, and budgets. That's why we're expanding the GPT-6 series with the launch of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra pioneered a new generation of intelligence, and these two new models further improve cost-effectiveness, bringing those advantages to a broader range of users. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using the same method we used to train GPT-6 Astra, distilling Astra's leading capabilities in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use, and model alignment into faster, more economical models.

The company stated that both new models outperform GPT-5.6, and are priced lower than Astra (as well as the GPT-5.6 version it replaces). For example, the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna are priced 50% lower than their GPT-5.6 counterparts.
